summary: LatticeWorks embeddings quality degradation causing multi-region failover and billing exposure - customer escalated
description: Issue summary: Starting 2024-11-07 14:05 UTC, LatticeWorks observed a sharp drop in embeddings similarity scores and a corresponding spike in 5xx errors when indexing new vectors. Traffic from their production clusters in us-east and eu-west triggered automated routing failovers to fallback embeddings variants, increasing latency and unit costs. Impact: Search relevance degraded across customer-facing features (recommendations, semantic search). Customer reported missing results and billing anomalies. Scope: Affected only LatticeWorks tenant on enterprise plan; cross-region failover caused billing exposure for both regions as requests were routed to quantized fallback models.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send batch embedding ingestion for ~1M vectors using customer API key in us-east
2) Observe elevated 5xx rate and degraded cosine similarity on comparator set
3) Watch routing decision logs for fallback selection to embed-quant-1
4) Confirm increased per-token/per-embed billing in customer invoice preview

comments: Support (Maya Chen) - 2024-11-07T14:12Z: Customer reported search results dropping to near-random and seeing 502/503 over last 7 minutes. Escalating to SRE and Applied ML. Opened incident INC-20241107-01.

SRE (Ravi Shah) - 2024-11-07T14:20Z: Noticed high KV cache eviction on open-embed-qa-2.1 pods in us-east. Eviction correlates with high ingestion rate spikes. Pinning additional pods to limit OOM churn; routing team investigating fallback rule triggers.

Applied ML (Nadia Lopez) - 2024-11-07T14:38Z: Initial hypothesis: quantized variant embed-quant-1 has different embedding distribution causing similarity shift. Need model-drift check and local repro against golden prompt set.

Customer (LatticeWorks - Samir Patel) - 2024-11-07T14:45Z: This is urgent. Production search is impacted. We need ETA for full restore and an explanation for billing jump. CSM requested immediate credits if billing cannot be limited.

Support (Maya Chen) - 2024-11-07T15:05Z: Applied temporary rate-limits on bulk ingestion for LatticeWorks and enabled canary routing to control traffic to quantized variants. Notified billing to hold invoices while we investigate.

SRE (Ravi Shah) - 2024-11-07T16:45Z: Root cause identified in kernel selection path where a new kernel rollout (PR #1987) introduced a failure path under high batch sizes causing fallback to embed-quant-1. Reverted PR and restarted affected pools; error rate falling.
Customer (Samir Patel) - 2024-11-07T17:10Z: Acknowledged restoration of service. Please confirm long-term mitigation and compensation plan.
investigation_notes: Timeline: Incident began at 14:05 UTC when bulk ingestion peaked. Automated fallback rules engaged within 30-90s.
Finding 1: Kernel-selection PR #1987 introduced a race when batch_size > 1024 resulting in kernel negotiation failures (KERN-503) causing routing to pick quantized fallback variants.

Finding 2: embed-quant-1 has distributional shift vs open-embed-qa-2.1 leading to low cosine similarity on LatticeWorks test vectors; quality regression not previously flagged by model onboarding tests.
Finding 3: Autoscaler heat-up + high eviction rate created pod churn, amplifying kernel negotiation failures.
Finding 4: Billing pipeline counted routed fallback requests at higher unit-cost; customer saw a preliminary invoice preview spike (~+34%).
Partial mitigations applied: PR revert, restart of affected pools, temporary ingestion rate-limits for customer key, billing hold placed pending review.
Monitoring gaps: No synthetic check that verifies similarity distribution after kernel change; routing tests only validated latency and error rates, not embedding quality.
Hypothesis validated by local repro and metric correlation graphs (kernel_error_rate vs fallback_rate vs cosine_mean).
resolution: Root cause: A kernel-selection change (PR #1987) created a failure path under large-batch ingest which triggered automated routing to quantized fallback variants. The quantized variant produced lower-quality embeddings for LatticeWorks' comparator set and increased billing. Fix: reverted PR #1987, restarted affected serving pools, enforced ingestion rate-limits for LatticeWorks, and held billing for impacted window. Deployed a hotfix to make kernel negotiation tolerant to large-batches and added a feature-flag gate for the kernel rollout. Customer was issued a credit equivalent to estimated excess charge and notified of the post-incident plan.
post_incident_actions: 1) Add similarity-distribution check to model onboarding and kernel rollout CI (owner: Applied ML, due 2024-11-22)
2) Modify routing policies to prefer degraded-quality safe-mode instead of costlier fallbacks in tenant-scoped incidents (owner: Runtime Routing, due 2024-11-15)
3) Introduce synthetic golden-set runs for top 100 enterprise customers during kernel/model rollouts (owner: Reliability, due 2024-12-01)
4) Revise autoscaler thresholds and add pod-stability guard to reduce eviction churn under bulk-ingest (owner: Infra, due 2024-11-20)
5) Update billing pipeline to mark disputed windows and surface provisional credits early (owner: Finance, due 2024-11-14)
6) Run a customer-facing post-incident review with LatticeWorks and provide final credit reconciliation (owner: CS, scheduled 2024-11-12)
7) Update embeddings playbook with rollback steps for kernel rollouts and a checklist to validate embedding quality (owner: OPS, done 2024-11-09)
8) Root-cause postmortem published to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-20241107-01 (owner: Incident Lead, done)
9) Retro: cross-team tabletop for kernel rollout (participants: Runtime, Applied ML, Reliability, Billing) scheduled 2024-11-18
customer_impact_summary: LatticeWorks production search relevance degraded for ~2.5 hours across us-east and eu-west; ingest pipelines experienced 5xxs and temporary increased unit cost due to fallback routing. Customer experienced user-facing errors and requested expedited credit resolution.
notes_for_followup: Ensure CSM has script for communicating provisional credits and expected timing
Confirm applied hotfix has been promoted through canary and does not regress under synthetic stress tests
Close coordination required between Reliability and Applied ML on future kernel/model rollouts
